correctness.rationale: Exact formula Z_k=Σ_i binom(r_i,k)/binom(n,k) follows by uniform subset counting. For each unequal occupancy pair the sign of successive retention-ratio difference equals sign of the explicit integer T_k, with strictly positive cleared denominator. The complete loops cover 3,654 pairs below 29 sites and 406 at 29, finding unique (22,26) with exactly two turns. Equal occupancies yield monotone (r-k)/(n-k). Witness fractions/differences were checked exactly, and direct enumeration of 146,595 subsets confirms its incidence interpretation. The all-species weighted-variance identity is derived algebraically and rationally spot checked. No extrapolation to n>29, noisy data, or all numbers of species is claimed.

originality.rationale: The 2014 source defines zeta diversity and interprets ratios; 2018 implementation supports the computation; 2019 work interprets increasing, asymptotic and modal retention curves. Primary full-text comparisons and indexed searches for equivalent binomial-mixture and nonunimodal zeta claims found no exact minimal 29-site two-species uniqueness theorem. This is a qualified originality judgement, not a proof from missing hits.
residual_risks: A previously unindexed two-species zeta ratio table or general total-positivity/binomial-mixture theorem could contain the same n=29 result.
The 2019 reported curve archetypes are descriptive and therefore should not be misread as an invalidated universal theorem.
Finite exact classification through n=29 supplies no universal upper bound on numbers of turns beyond that range.

value.rationale: Retention rates are an established ecological descriptor for comparing compositional change across numbers of habitats (McGeoch et al. 2019). A sharp first occurrence with only two species isolates the simplest possible heterogeneity mechanism for a valley followed by a peak, while ruling that qualitative pattern out at all smaller site counts. The exact occupancy-variance minus finite-site-depletion criterion identifies why directions can switch and is applicable to arbitrary species richness. Tiny exact changes and restriction to all-subsets averaging are explicitly disclosed; novelty of the arithmetic alone is not the value rationale.
